title: India’s Startup D-Propulse Ignites Detonation Future — TRL-5 Breakthrough in Supersonic Propulsion
summary: Indian startup D-Propulse released video footage of short-duration runs of an air-breathing rotating detonation prototype at a government facility on July 21-22, 2026. Tests reportedly produced a 5 kN burn with reduced air mass flow and reduced fuel flow. The company frames the work as a TRL-5 milestone for supersonic propulsion.
content:
Thought I'll give you guys a sneak peek. Here's a video of one of the short duration runs conducted by @dpropulse with its air-breathing rotating detonation prototype at a government facility during July 21-22, 2026. 5 kN burn with reduced air mass flow and reduced fuel flow as… pic.twitter.com/wx6da8LWZ5

The footage, posted by the company, shows brief test firings of a rotating detonation engine — an air-breathing detonation-based propulsion concept aimed at higher efficiency and performance for high-speed flight. The post and title claim the program has reached a TRL-5 breakthrough in supersonic propulsion, indicating subsystem validation in a relevant environment.

No further technical specifications, long-duration run results, or official government statements were provided in the post. The available report lists the author as unknown and the publication timestamp corresponds to 2026-07-26T07:08:00Z. Observers note the tests were short-duration runs and shared as a sneak-peek video rather than a formal technical release.
